Article 99 permits fines of up to €35 million or, for an undertaking, 7% of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher; the exact caveat is that the percentage applies to undertakings and the amount imposed depends on the circumstances.

assessment.rationale: The closest contemporaneous evidence does not support the stated figure: Deloitte Legal Germany’s 2024 survey of 500 company managers found that only 26.2% had begun seriously addressing AI Act implementation, while 48.6% had not seriously prepared. That is materially below “about 40%,” and the evidence concerns German companies rather than all European companies, making the claim’s broader geographic wording unsupported. Some surveys use different populations and looser measures of readiness, but they do not establish the claim as phrased by year-end 2024.

assessment.rationale: The claim accurately states the maximum percentage-based penalty for non-compliance with the EU AI Act’s prohibited-practices rules. Article 99 permits fines of up to €35 million or, for an undertaking, 7% of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher; the exact caveat is that the percentage applies to undertakings and the amount imposed depends on the circumstances.

claims.claim: Fines for prohibited practices under the EU AI Act can reach 7% of global annual turnover.

assessment.rationale: The closest contemporaneous evidence does not support the stated figure: Deloitte Legal Germany’s 2024 survey of 500 company managers found that only 26.2% had begun seriously addressing AI Act implementation, while 48.6% had not seriously prepared. That is materially below “about 40%,” and the evidence concerns German companies rather than all European companies, making the claim’s broader geographic wording unsupported. Some surveys use different populations and looser measures of readiness, but they do not establish the claim as phrased by year-end 2024.
